subtopic: Pipeline parallelism / Layer partition and bubble
learningObjective: Explain how pipeline parallelism shards a model across devices and what causes pipeline bubbles.
stem: Pipeline parallelism (PP) with P stages splits a model's layers across P devices. Which characterization of PP for LLM inference is correct?

options.text: PP partitions layers into P contiguous groups, one per device. In decode inference, a single-request forward passes sequentially through P stages, so per-request latency is not reduced (only memory is shared); throughput improves only with multiple in-flight requests, and imbalanced stages create bubbles.

PP partitions attention heads across devices (like TP) but with additional latency-hiding across P forward passes; per-token latency in decode is P times faster than a single-device baseline because P stages run concurrently.

In inference, PP has no bubble because there is no backward pass; a single request can flow through all P stages with perfectly overlapped stage execution, and per-token latency drops by P× under any load.

Each PP stage holds a copy of the full model and processes different tokens of the same request in parallel; the pipeline works because each token can be processed independently along the layer dimension after residual connections.

explanation: PP partitions the model layer-wise: each device holds a contiguous group of layers. For a single request in decode, the forward is sequential across stages, so per-token latency is not reduced (in fact slightly increased by inter-stage transfer). PP improves throughput only by running multiple requests through the pipeline in parallel (each stage is busy with a different request at each moment). Imbalanced stage compute or memory creates 'bubbles' where some devices idle. In inference the backward-pass bubble of training does not exist, but pipeline scheduling still matters.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: layer-partition, sequential forward for one request, throughput-oriented benefit.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: describes something like TP, not PP; PP does not speed up single-request decode.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: single-request latency is not reduced by PP.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: PP does not replicate the model; each stage holds only its layer group.

assumptions: Standard layer-wise PP as in GPipe / PipeDream / Megatron-LM.
Stage transfer overhead is small relative to stage compute.
nonImplications: Does not imply PP is useless; it is essential when the model does not fit on one device.
Does not imply zero bubble; imbalance and inter-stage latency still create idle time.

performanceClaim.scope: Pipeline parallelism for LLM inference: layer partition, throughput vs latency
